subject: Energy
title: Electric Vehicle Charging and the Grid
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Electric Vehicle Charging and the Grid.

hook.text: Millions of EVs will need charging—potentially adding enormous demand to local distribution networks.

buildup.text: A Level 2 home charger draws 7–19 kW—equivalent to adding 2–5 extra houses of demand on one circuit.

discovery.text: DC fast chargers pull 50–350 kW—a single station can stress a local transformer beyond its rated capacity.

twist.text: Smart charging schedules EVs to charge at night when demand is low—turning a problem into grid-balancing opportunity.

climax.text: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) lets EVs feed power back—turning millions of car batteries into a virtual power plant.

punchline.text: EVs strain the grid—or support it, depending on when they charge.

quiz.question: What is vehicle-to-grid (V2G)?
